title: Pequash (Goldsmith's Neck)
summary: Pequash is a Cutchogue placename for a neck of land known as Goldsmith's Neck, interpreted as open or cleared ground.
map_geometry_source: Approximate Cutchogue-area point used as a general proxy for Goldsmith's Neck; exact neck boundary needs local map review.
history_content: Pequash belongs to the Cutchogue neck-and-farm landscape on the North Fork. The exact extent of Goldsmith's Neck needs local geographic and title research.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as open level ground, clear land, or a clearing. Quasha is a later cross-reference spelling that should be kept with this placename.

Why Place Names Matter

“When people name places, they symbolically take possession of them, stamping them with the imprimatur of their own culture, history, and identity.”

— Jamie Eves, 'Swift Waters' or 'Cedar Swamp'? The Meaning of 'Willimantic' and Other Indigenous Place Names in Connecticut (n.d.), article discussion, paragraph beginning 'Despite these problems'
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point near Cutchogue for Goldsmith's Neck. This marker is not an exact historic boundary or parcel location.
